content: CYBER INCIDENT MANAGEMENT (CIM) CYBIL PORTAL RESOURCES GUIDE Last Updated: October 2022 Summary The Cyber Incident Management (CIM) Cybil Portal Resources Guide is an initiative of the GFCE Working Group B CIM Task Force. Context During the June 2022 in-person GFCE CIM TF Meeting in the margins of the 34th Annual FIRST Conference, members of the CIM TF examined and discussed the Cybil Portal resources that were under the topic of the Task Force (Cyber Incident Management) on the Cybil Knowledge Portal. After careful consideration and revision of all these resources, the Task Force decided to continue this discussion by adding those who they found relevant and were missing to the Cybil Portal and ultimately creating a useful and simple guide for the Task Force and the CIM Community in general. Aim The objective of this guide is to provide an overview of all the resources that are available for the CIM community on the Cybil Portal as of October 2022. By doing this, we hope that users of the Cybil Portal will be able to navigate through all the cyber incident management resources available in an easier and more focused manner. Information Sharing This guide intends to help users build their cyber capacity according to their various different needs. The resources are classified into different practical sections so that users can adapt them to their different needs. This way, if users want to, for instance, find out tools and resources that will help them build a CSIRT or want to measure their organisational incident management maturity, they can freely make use of the most relevant resources available in the field. metadata.title: Cyber Incident Management (CIM) Cybil Portal Resources Guide

additional_metadata.General information about Best Practices: The Cyber Incident Management (CIM) Cybil Portal Resources Guide is an initiative of the GFCE Working Group B CIM Task Force. The objective of this guide is to provide an overview of all the resources that are available for the CIM community on the Cybil Portal as of October 2022. By doing this, we hope that users of the Cybil Portal will be able to navigate through all the cyber incident management resources available in an easier and more focused manner. In addition, this guide intends to help users build their cyber capacity according to their various different needs. For this reason, the resources are classified into different practical sections so that users can adapt them to their different needs. This way, if users want to, for instance, find out tools and resources that will help them build a CSIRT or want to measure their organisational incident management maturity, they can freely make use of the most relevant resources available in the field.
additional_metadata.Time coverage: The guide was last updated in October 2022, and the included resources date from 2015 to 2022, aligning with your post-2015 requirement.
additional_metadata.Geographic coverage:
Global in scope, but with strong focus on GFCE member states, including EU27 countries, Western Balkans, Africa, Latin America, and ASEAN regions.
Specific tools from ENISA, EUROPOL, GFCE, and other European stakeholders ensure high relevance to EU and associated countries.
additional_metadata.Primary objective: To enhance global and national cybersecurity readiness by consolidating, classifying, and disseminating high-quality resources for Cyber Incident Management (CIM) through the Cybil Portal—targeting both civilian and defence-aligned stakeholders.
additional_metadata.Secondary objective:
Enable governments and organisations to establish and mature CSIRTs/SOCs (Computer Security Incident Response Teams / Security Operations Centres).
Foster standardisation of incident response procedures and maturity assessments globally.
Promote accessible capacity-building tools for low- and middle-income countries and regions.
Support knowledge exchange and reduce asymmetries in cybersecurity readiness.
additional_metadata.Implementation strategy:
Aggregation of relevant reports, guides, frameworks, and tools from trusted global and regional partners (e.g. ENISA, FIRST, GFCE, ITU, MITRE).
Classification into thematic categories: CSIRT development, maturity frameworks, threat intelligence, incident response, strategy/policy, etc.
Continuous curation by the GFCE Working Group B – CIM Task Force.
Hosting on the Cybil Portal to ensure open access and easy navigation.
Feedback loop from the global CIM community to identify gaps and add relevant resources.
additional_metadata.Success factors:
Broad stakeholder involvement: input from ENISA, FIRST.org, MITRE, NCSC NL, Europol, etc.
Usability-first design: thematic resource classification makes adoption easier for practitioners.
Credibility of sources: only validated and reputable tools/guides are included.
Global reach with EU alignment, ensuring both relevance and scalability.
additional_metadata.Challenges:
Variable uptake and application: success depends on whether national stakeholders engage with and apply the resources.
Language and localisation barriers in some regions.
Sustainability: requires continued curation, funding, and community involvement to remain relevant and up to date.
Limited real-time coordination: focuses on preparedness and learning rather than live response coordination.
additional_metadata.Alignment with EU Policies:
Aligned with EU Cybersecurity Strategy, NIS2 Directive, and ENISA capacity-building initiatives.
Supports the EU’s goals for standardised response capabilities, improved threat preparedness, and cross-border collaboration.
Reinforces efforts within the EU Cybersecurity Act, particularly the push for maturity frameworks and CSIRT network strengthening.
additional_metadata.Transferability:
Highly transferable across geographies, sectors, and organisation types.
Effective for both national-level policymakers and technical implementers.
Especially adaptable to countries with emerging cybersecurity ecosystems.
The portal can be replicated or mirrored in regional or sectoral platforms.
additional_metadata.Comment: This is a top-tier, fully mature, and replicable best practice, ideal for dual-use cybersecurity coordination in both national and EU-level strategies. It represents a gold standard in law enforcement-led cyber threat governance.
Joint Cyber Incident Response Teams, Real-Time Threat Intelligence Sharing Platforms, Integrated Crisis Management Frameworks, Shared Resource Allocation, Cybersecurity Governance Framework, Public-Private Cybersecurity Partnerships, National Cybersecurity Simulations, Cross-Sector Crisis Management, Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Workshops, Collaborative Threat Intelligence Networks, Develop Unified Policy Frameworks, Leverage International Best Practices, Trust-Building Activities, Vulnerability and Threat Analysis Policies, Shared Funding and Resources, Unified Threat Intelligence (TI) and Early Warning Systems, Cross-Sector Vulnerability Disclosure Mechanisms.

✗ Lack of awareness capacity,
✗ Lack of dual-use technologies,
✓ Lack of coordinated cybersecurity policies,

✓ Cultural differences between the two sectors.
